title: Fernwood Health Sprint Planning - Patient Portal Redesign

transcript.speaker: Ines Alvarez
transcript.text: This sprint we're kicking off the patient portal redesign. Ben, you wanted to weigh in on scope before we commit.

transcript.speaker: Ben Holloway
transcript.text: Right - the main ask from support is that patients can't easily find past lab results. Whatever we do this sprint, that needs to be in scope.

transcript.speaker: Ines Alvarez
transcript.text: Agreed, that's item one on my list. The redesign also includes a new appointment scheduling widget, but that could slip to next sprint if needed.

transcript.speaker: Liam Fitzgerald
transcript.text: From a backend angle, surfacing lab results faster means we need a new indexed endpoint - the current query joins five tables and takes almost four seconds for patients with a long history.

transcript.speaker: Ines Alvarez
transcript.text: Can you get that endpoint done this sprint?

transcript.speaker: Liam Fitzgerald
transcript.text: Yes, I'll have the indexed lab-results endpoint ready by Wednesday next week.

transcript.speaker: Amara Okafor
transcript.text: I want to flag a risk - that table gets heavy write traffic from the lab integration nightly batch. Adding an index could slow those writes down. I'd like to test it in staging under realistic load before it hits production.

transcript.speaker: Ines Alvarez
transcript.text: Good call. Liam, once it's built, can you and Amara run a load test together?

transcript.speaker: Liam Fitzgerald
transcript.text: Sure, we can do that Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Ines Alvarez
transcript.text: Let's make the appointment scheduling widget a stretch goal - if the lab results work finishes early, we start on it, but it's not this sprint's commitment.

transcript.speaker: Ben Holloway
transcript.text: Agreed, don't let it distract from the core scope.

transcript.speaker: Ines Alvarez
transcript.text: One open question I don't have an answer to yet - should lab results older than two years be paginated separately, or all loaded at once? I need to check with clinical on whether providers ever need to see that far back quickly.

transcript.speaker: Ben Holloway
transcript.text: I don't know either, good to flag. Loop in clinical this week.

summary_key_points: This sprint's core commitment is faster access to past lab results in the patient portal
A new indexed lab-results endpoint is needed to replace a slow five-table join
The nightly lab integration batch's write performance needs testing before the index goes to production
The appointment scheduling widget is a stretch goal, not a firm commitment, this sprint

action_items.task: Build the indexed lab-results endpoint by Wednesday next week
Run a load test of the new index against the nightly batch with Amara on Thursday
Run a load test of the new index against the nightly batch with Liam on Thursday
Loop in the clinical team this week on whether old lab results need separate pagination

decisions: Make the appointment scheduling widget a stretch goal rather than a firm sprint commitment
open_questions: Should lab results older than two years be paginated separately, or all loaded at once?
